title: Hourly usage rollup correction and NetSuite export normalization
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported invoice mismatches between Stripe preview and final invoice after usage-based hourly pricing, and Finance flagged a reconciliation delta in NetSuite exports. Root causes traced to (1) inconsistent proration/rounding logic between the usage-aggregation pipeline and the Stripe invoicing payload, (2) multi-currency fractional-cent handling, and (3) the nightly NetSuite CSV export normalizer truncating memo fields and dropping deferred revenue mapping lines when retries happen. This ticket centralizes the fixes: correct the hourly rollup/rounding, make Stripe previews match final invoices, and harden the NetSuite export pipeline so exported rows are idempotent, complete, and map to the current accounting schema.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduceable end-to-end test showing Stripe preview equals final invoice for hourly usage PRs (same set of inputs) across USD and EUR with daylight-savings boundary cases
NetSuite export files for a 30-day window match expected ledger lines: no missing memo fields, deferred revenue lines present, and mapping keys align with Finance schema v2025.11
Reconciliation delta reduced to < $5 across a sampled set of 500 customer accounts for the previous 60 days
Nightly billing export job becomes idempotent: rerunning the same window produces identical output and does not create duplicate NetSuite records
Canary rollout (5% of accounts) for 48 hours with monitoring (billing disparity dashboard) before full roll-out
investigation_notes: 2025-11-12: Initial incident — Finance reported +$1,482 unexplained ledger variance for 2025-10 invoices; support ticket IDs #SUP-1829 and #SUP-1833 with affected accounts attached

2025-11-13: Reproduced locally: hourly-usage aggregator uses banker's rounding (round-to-even) when computing prorated cents; Stripe API expects round half-up when converting fractional tokens to cents in some endpoints — causes 1c differences on many small invoices

2025-11-14: Found multi-currency conversion pipeline applies FX at invoice-creation time but proration happens on pre-conversion values leading to double-rounding; observed EUR accounts with >10% of invoices off by 1-2 EUR cents after conversion

2025-11-15: NetSuite export normalizer (legacy python script) splits CSV on commas and truncates memo fields > 256 chars; also retry logic replays partial exports and omits deferredRevenue lines when a previous partial file exists
2025-11-16: Stripe API 429s (rate limiting) during heavy export windows cause partial invoice fetches; current export job does not checkpoint pulled-invoice IDs so subsequent run misses those IDs

2025-11-18: Investigated timezone boundary bug: hourly buckets anchored to account creation timezone rather than UTC bucket start — caused overlapping buckets and duplicated usage lines for ~0.3% customers at DST transitions
proposed_solution: Centralize proration logic into billing-core service and publish API used by both invoice preview and final invoice pipelines so logic is single source of truth
Change rounding strategy to smallest-currency-unit rounding with half-up semantics for all endpoints; add canonical rounding util with tests for USD/EUR/JPY

Apply proration on post-conversion values for multi-currency flows to avoid double-rounding: convert usage units to currency at the time-of-usage or use FX-locked conversions and store cents as integers

Migrate NetSuite export from comma-CSV to newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with explicit field escaping and a schema version header; include export manifest with exported invoice IDs to make export runs idempotent

Add robust checkpointing: persist set of invoice IDs successfully exported per-run; implement 5xx/429 exponential backoff with full jitter for Stripe calls and adaptive batch sizes to reduce the chance of 429s
Fix timezone bucket anchoring to use account.active_billing_timezone with UTC-aligned hourly windows; add extra unit tests around DST transitions

Create reconciliation harness that compares: (a) aggregated ledger from export NDJSON, (b) Stripe invoice line items via API, and (c) finance expected totals. Run across 60-day history and generate report for Finance
Add a migration script to reprocess invoices in the 60-day window and emit corrected NetSuite-ready ndjson files for Finance ingestion, with clear pack-and-upload instructions in Confluence
